e.g. `"refactor.extract.function"`.

The set of kinds is open and client needs to announce the kinds it supports
to the server during initialization.
You can make your own code action kinds, the ones supported by LSP are:
- `quickfix`
- `refactor`
  - `refactor.extract`
  - `refactor.inline`
  - `refactor.rewrite`
- `source` Source code actions apply to the entire file. Eg fixing all issues or organising imports.
  - `source.organizeImports`
  - `source.fixAll`

doc:
`$/lean/rpc/call` client->server request.

A request to execute a procedure bound for RPC.
If an incorrect session ID is present, the server errors with `RpcNeedsReconnect`.

Extends `TextDocumentPositionParams` because in Lean,
symbols exist in the context of a position within a source file
(e.g., `foo` is defined below but not above `def foo`).
We use the position to resolve the set of defined constants,
registered RPC methods, etc.

Both the request and the response may contain `RpcEncodable` data.
It is serialized following the `RpcWireFormat`.

`$/lean/rpc/connect` client<-server reply.

Indicates that an RPC connection had been made and a session started for it.

`$/lean/rpc/connect` client->server request.

Starts an RPC session at the given file's worker, replying with the new session ID.

RPC requests for that session will reply with `RpcNeedsReconnect` errors. The client should discard
references held from that session and `connect` again.

  | some tag =>
    match tag with
    | "renamed" =>

        let a_1 ← Lean.fromJson? jsons[1]!
        pure (Lean.Lsp.OpenNamespace.renamed a a_1)
    | "allExcept" =>
      (json.parseCtorFields "allExcept" 2 (some #[`namespace, `exceptions])).bind fun jsons => do
        let a ← Lean.fromJson? jsons[0]!
        let a_1 ← Lean.fromJson? jsons[1]!
        pure (Lean.Lsp.OpenNamespace.allExcept a a_1)
    | x => Except.error "no inductive constructor matched"
  | none => Except.error "no inductive tag found"

      { id := Lean.JsonRpc.RequestID.num (Lean.JsonNumber.fromNat requestNo),

    Lean.Lsp.Ipc.readResponseAs (Lean.JsonRpc.RequestID.num (Lean.JsonNumber.fromNat requestNo))
        (Option (Array Lean.Lsp.CallHierarchyItem))

  have roots : Array Lean.Lsp.CallHierarchyItem := r.result.getD #[]
  have hierarchies : Array Lean.Lsp.Ipc.CallHierarchy := #[]
  let __s ←
    forIn roots (requestNo, hierarchies) fun root __s =>
        have requestNo := __s.1;
        have hierarchies := __s.2;
        do
        let __x ← Lean.Lsp.Ipc.expandOutgoingCallHierarchy.go✝ requestNo root #[] ∅
        match __x with
          | (hierarchy, rootRequestNo) =>
            have requestNo := rootRequestNo;
            have hierarchies := hierarchies.push hierarchy;
            pure (ForInStep.yield (requestNo, hierarchies))
  have requestNo : ℕ := __s.1

fun waitForILeansId target version => do
  Lean.Lsp.Ipc.writeRequest
      { id := waitForILeansId, method := "$/lean/waitForILeans",
        param := { uri? := some target, version? := some version } }
  let __s ←
    forIn { } (none, ()) fun x __s =>
        if true = true then do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Lsp.Ipc.readMessage
          match __do_lift with
            | Lean.JsonRpc.Message.response id result =>
              if (id == waitForILeansId) = true then pure (ForInStep.done (some (), ()))
              else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
            | Lean.JsonRpc.Message.responseError id code msg data? =>
              if (id == waitForILeansId) = true then do
                throw (IO.userError (toString "Waiting for ILeans failed: " ++ toString msg))
                pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
              else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
            | x => pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
        else pure (ForInStep.done (none, ()))
  have __r : Option Unit × Unit := __s
  match __r.1 with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => pure ()

doc:
Merges a new `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notification into a previously accumulated one.

- If there is no previous notification, the new one is used as-is.
- If `isIncremental?` is `true`, the new diagnostics are appended.
- Otherwise the new notification replaces the previous one.

The returned params always have `isIncremental? := some false` since they represent the full
accumulated set.

value.text:
fun prev? next =>
  (have replace :=
      { uri := next.uri, version? := next.version?, isIncremental? := some false,
        diagnostics := next.diagnostics };
    match prev? with
    | some prev =>
      if next.isIncremental?.getD false = true then
        pure
          { uri := next.uri, version? := next.version?, isIncremental? := some false,
            diagnostics := prev.diagnostics ++ next.diagnostics }
      else pure replace
    | x => pure replace).run

doc:
Yields the file source of `item` by attempting to obtain `mod : Name` from `item.data?`. \
Panics if `item.data?` is not present or does not contain a `mod` field and the first element of a
`data?` array cannot be parsed to `Name`.
Used when `completionItem/resolve` requests pass the watchdog to decide which file worker to forward
the request to.
Since this function can panic and clients typically send `completionItem/resolve` requests for every
selected completion item, all completion items returned by the server in `textDocument/completion`
requests must have a `data?` field that has a `mod` field.

      | Lean.Json.arr elems => do
        let __do_lift ← data.getArrVal? 0
        Lean.fromJson? __do_lift
      | x => throw (toString "unexpected completion item data: " ++ toString data)
    | x => throw (toString "no data param on completion item " ++ toString item.label);
  match r with
  | Except.ok id => id

    Lean.Elab.ContextInfo →
      Lean.Elab.Info →

          List (Lean.Elab.HoverableInfoPrio × Lean.Elab.InfoWithCtx) →

fun {m} [Monad m] t hoverPos includeStop filter =>
  have postNode := fun ctx info children results => do
    let results ← filter ctx info children (List.filterMap (fun r? => r?.join) results)
    have maxPrio? : Option Lean.Elab.HoverableInfoPrio := (List.map (fun x => x.1) results).max?
    have bestResult? : Option (Lean.Elab.HoverableInfoPrio × Lean.Elab.InfoWithCtx) :=
      List.find? (fun x => some x.1 == maxPrio?) results
    match bestResult? with
      | some (prio, i) => pure (some (prio, i))
      | x =>
        have isAuxInfo :=
          info.stx.isOfKind Lean.nullKind ||
            Option.any (fun x => x.elaborator == `Lean.Elab.Tactic.evalWithAnnotateState)
              info.toElabInfo?;
        if isAuxInfo = true then pure none
        else
          have isEligibleInfoKind :=
            (match info with
              | Lean.Elab.Info.ofFieldInfo i => true
              | Lean.Elab.Info.ofOptionInfo i => true
              | Lean.Elab.Info.ofErrorNameInfo i => true
              | x => false) ||
              info.toElabInfo?.isSome;
          match info.stx.getRange? true with
          | some r =>
            if (!r.contains hoverPos includeStop || !isEligibleInfoKind) = true then pure none
            else
              have priority :=
                { isHoverPosOnStop := r.stop == hoverPos, size := r.start.byteDistance r.stop,
                  isVariableInfo :=
                    match info with
                    |
                    Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo
                        { elaborator := elaborator, stx := stx, lctx := lctx,
                          expectedType? := expectedType?, expr := Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId,
                          isBinder := isBinder, isDisplayableTerm := isDisplayableTerm } =>
                      true
                    | x => false,
                  isPartialTermInfo :=
                    match info with
                    | Lean.Elab.Info.ofPartialTermInfo i => true
                    | x => false };
              have result := { ctx := ctx, info := info, children := children };
              pure (some (priority, result))
          | x => pure none;
  do
  let results ← Lean.Elab.InfoTree.visitM (fun x x_1 x_2 => pure true) postNode none t
  have bestResult? : Option Lean.Elab.InfoWithCtx := Option.map (fun x => x.2) results.join
  have __do_jp : Unit → m (Option Lean.Elab.InfoWithCtx) := fun __r => pure bestResult?

    | some bestResult =>
      match bestResult.info with
      | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo ti =>
        if ti.expr.isSyntheticSorry = true then pure none else __do_jp ()
      | x => __do_jp ()
    | x => __do_jp ()

fun i =>

  | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo ti => do
    let e ← Lean.instantiateMVars ti.expr
    if e.isSort = true then pure (none, none)
      else do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType e
        let tp ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
        let tpFmt ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr tp

          | Lean.Expr.const c us => do
            let eFmt ← Lean.PrettyPrinter.ppSignature c
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Info.fmtHover?.fmtModule?✝ c

                      infos := eFmt.infos },
                  __do_lift)
          | x => do
            let eFmt ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr e
            let lctx ← Lean.getLCtx
            have showTerm : Bool :=

              else tpFmt
            pure

                    { fmt := Std.format "```lean\n" ++ Std.format fmt ++ Std.format "\n```",
                      infos := ∅ },

    let tp ← Lean.Meta.inferType fi.val
    let tpFmt ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr tp
    pure

              fmt :=
                Std.format "```lean\n" ++ Std.format fi.fieldName ++ Std.format " : " ++
                    Std.format tpFmt ++

doc:
Elaborator information with elaborator context.

It can be thought of as a "thunked" elaboration computation that allows us
to retroactively extract type information, symbol locations, etc.
through arbitrary invocations of `runMetaM` (where the necessary context and state
can be reconstructed from `ctx` and `info.lctx`).

W.r.t. widgets, this is used to tag different parts of expressions in `ppExprTagged`.
This is the input to the RPC call `Lean.Widget.InteractiveDiagnostics.infoToInteractive`.
It carries over information about delaborated
`Info` nodes in a `CodeWithInfos`, and the associated pretty-printing
functionality is purpose-specific to showing the contents of infoview popups.

For use in standard LSP go-to-definition (see `Lean.Server.FileWorker.locationLinksOfInfo`),
all the elaborator information we need for similar tasks is already fully recoverable via
the `InfoTree` structure (see `Lean.Elab.InfoTree.visitM`).
There we use this as a convenience wrapper for queried nodes (e.g. the return value of
`Lean.Elab.InfoTree.hoverableInfoAt?`). It also includes the children info nodes
as additional context (this is unused in the RPC case, as delaboration has no notion of child nodes).

NOTE: This type is for internal use in the infoview/LSP. It should not be used in user widgets.

doc:
Try to retrieve `TacticInfo` for `hoverPos`.
We retrieve all `TacticInfo` nodes s.t. `hoverPos` is inside the node's range plus trailing whitespace.
We usually prefer the innermost such nodes so that for composite tactics such as `induction`, we show the nested proofs' states.
However, if `hoverPos` is after the tactic, we prefer nodes that are not indented relative to it, meaning that e.g. at `|` in
```lean
have := by
  exact foo
|
```
we show the (final, see below) state of `have`, not `exact`.

Moreover, we instruct the LSP server to use the state after tactic execution if
- the hover position is after the info's start position *and*
- there is no nested tactic info after the hover position (tactic combinators should decide for themselves
  where to show intermediate states by calling `withTacticInfoContext`)

  (hoverPos : String.Pos.Raw) : List Lean.Elab.GoalsAtResult

value.text:
fun text t hoverPos =>
  have gs :=
    Lean.Elab.InfoTree.collectNodesBottomUp
      (fun ctx i cs gs =>
        (match i with
          | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTacticInfo ti =>
            match (i.pos?, i.tailPos?) with
            | (some pos, some tailPos) =>
              have trailSize := i.stx.getTrailingSize;
              have atEOF := tailPos.byteIdx + trailSize == text.source.rawEndPos.byteIdx;
              have __do_jp := fun __r => pure gs;
              if
                  pos ≤ hoverPos ∧
                    (decide (hoverPos.byteIdx < tailPos.byteIdx + max 1 trailSize) || atEOF) =
                      true then
                if
                    (gs.isEmpty || decide (hoverPos ≥ tailPos) && gs.all fun x => x.indented) =
                      true then
                  pure
                    [{ ctxInfo := ctx, tacticInfo := ti,
                        useAfter :=
                          decide (hoverPos > pos) &&
                            !cs.any
                                (Lean.Elab.InfoTree.goalsAt?.hasNestedTactic✝ hoverPos pos tailPos),
                        indented :=
                          decide ((text.toPosition pos).column > (text.toPosition hoverPos).column),
                        priority :=
                          if (hoverPos.byteIdx == tailPos.byteIdx + trailSize) = true then 0
                          else 1 }]
                else __do_jp ()
              else __do_jp ()
            | x => pure gs
          | x => pure gs).run)
      t;
  have maxPrio? := (List.map (fun x => x.priority) gs).max?;
  List.filter (fun x => some x.priority == maxPrio?) gs

{
  compare := fun i1 i2 =>
    (if (i1.isHoverPosOnStop && !i2.isHoverPosOnStop) = true then pure Ordering.lt
      else
        if (!i1.isHoverPosOnStop && i2.isHoverPosOnStop) = true then pure Ordering.gt
        else
          if i1.size > i2.size then pure Ordering.lt
          else
            if i1.size < i2.size then pure Ordering.gt
            else
              if (i1.isVariableInfo && !i2.isVariableInfo) = true then pure Ordering.lt
              else
                if (!i1.isVariableInfo && i2.isVariableInfo) = true then pure Ordering.gt
                else
                  if (i1.isPartialTermInfo && !i2.isPartialTermInfo) = true then pure Ordering.lt
                  else
                    if (!i1.isPartialTermInfo && i2.isPartialTermInfo) = true then pure Ordering.gt
                    else pure Ordering.eq).run }

Fold an info tree as follows, while ensuring that the correct `ContextInfo` is supplied at each stage:

* Nodes are combined with the initial value `init` using `f`, and the result is then combined with the children using a left fold
* On InfoTree holes, we just return the initial value.

This is like `InfoTree.foldInfo`, but it also passes the whole node to `f` instead of just the head.

fun {m} {α} [Monad m] t f =>
  Lean.Elab.InfoTree.foldInfoM
    (fun ctx info result =>
      match info with
      | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo ti => do
        let __do_lift ← f ctx ti
        match __do_lift with
          | some a => pure (a :: result)
          | none => pure result
      | x => pure result)
    [] t

fun i =>
  match i with
  | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo ti => do
    let a ← Lean.Meta.inferType ti.expr
    pure (some a)
  | Lean.Elab.Info.ofFieldInfo fi => do
    let a ← Lean.Meta.inferType fi.val
    pure (some a)
  | Lean.Elab.Info.ofDelabTermInfo ti => do
    let a ← Lean.Meta.inferType ti.expr
    pure (some a)
  | x => pure none
